- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment transition.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in the first 7–10 days; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to early horizon (days 1–10).
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 values, model tends to drift toward mean; apply a “sentiment smoothing” rule: average recent 3–5 sentiment values to adjust forecast baseline.
